title: Guests on SW2 cannot obtain leases
scenario: In this isolated branch variation, one guest on SW1 works and a guest on SW2 fails. Both access ports are in active VLAN 20. R1 is the DHCP server behind SW1 Gi0/1; its pool has free addresses. Before a change, both clients obtained correct leases.

exhibits.title: Representative SW2 trunk state
exhibits.text:
Po1 trunking; native VLAN 999
Allowed VLANs: 10,99,999
VLAN 20: active in local VLAN database
Guest access port Fa0/2: VLAN 20, connected

exhibits.title: Representative SW1 state
exhibits.text:
Po1 allowed VLANs: 10,20,99,999
Gi0/1 allowed/active/forwarding VLANs: 10,20,99,999
Local VLAN 20 client: valid DHCP lease

question: Which demonstrated change is needed on the SW2 path?
options: Add a DHCP helper to the management SVI
Change the native VLAN to the guest VLAN
Move the DHCP pool to the external router
explanation: SW2’s logical trunk excludes the client VLAN. The functioning local guest and healthy router trunk help isolate the failed path to the inter-switch link; a local VLAN entry alone does not place it in the trunk’s allowed list.
fix:
On this lab switch, restore the intended list and inspect member/logical consistency:

```ios
SW2# configure terminal
SW2(config)# interface port-channel1
SW2(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,99,999
SW2(config-if)# end
SW2# show interfaces trunk
SW2# show etherchannel summary
SW2# show spanning-tree vlan 20
```

Verify the VLAN is forwarding, renew the SW2 client and confirm the actual lease and gateway. Do not change the working DHCP server. Then confirm a fresh guest external HTTP request succeeds and a guest-initiated staff ping remains denied. Record the new client address if renewal changed it.

title: HQ routes are missing despite an established neighbor
scenario: R1 and R2 are the only routers on a dedicated Ethernet transit. The approved design uses point-to-point at both ends. Both required LAN interfaces are enabled in area 0 and passive. HQ access failed after an image migration. The following authored evidence was collected.

exhibits.title: Representative R1 observations
exhibits.text:
Gi0/1: Network Type POINT_TO_POINT; Hello 10; Dead 40
Neighbor 2.2.2.2: FULL
Required HQ route: absent

exhibits.title: Representative R2 observations
exhibits.text:
Gi0/0: Network Type BROADCAST; Hello 10; Dead 40
Required HQ interface: up/up, enabled in OSPF area 0
Intended transit network type: point-to-point

question: Which repair addresses the explicit configuration inconsistency?
options: Make the transit passive at both routers
Change both local process IDs to the same value
Restore point-to-point on R2’s transit interface
Redistribute all connected routes on both routers
explanation: The interfaces disagree about the OSPF topology model. Cisco documents route-calculation failures with such mismatches even when a FULL relationship is observed. The conclusion relies on the displayed types and intended design, not FULL alone.
fix:
Restore the intended type on R2:

```ios
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0
R2(config-if)# ip ospf network point-to-point
R2(config-if)# end
R2# show ip ospf interface gigabitethernet0/0
R2# show ip ospf neighbor
R2# show ip route
```

Allow convergence, compare R1’s type and routes, then test HQ and its return path. If the route remains absent, continue with advertisement and route-selection evidence instead of assuming this one change proves service. From the authorized staff client, repeat the original HQ ping and numeric/name HTTP to the external server. Keep the guest-to-HQ denial intact.

title: Guests receive leases but cannot use external HTTP
scenario: Guest gateway ping and external HTTP stopped after a named ACL edit. Staff service still works. GUEST-IN is inbound on R1 Gi0/0.20. The intended policy denies guest requests to staff, permits guest DHCP and permits external access.

exhibits.title: Authored before/after probe record
exhibits.text:
Guest DHCP renewal: succeeds
Line 35 count before new gateway/external probes: 40
Line 35 count after probes: 48
Staff external HTTP: succeeds

question: Which minimal repair preserves the intended restrictions?
options: Remove the inbound attachment of GUEST-IN
Permit all sources in R2’s NAT selection ACL
Add a second default route on the guest PC
explanation: The broad sequence 35 matches the failing requests before the intended entries. DHCP survives because an earlier permit matches it. Removing the whole list would also remove the required staff protection.
fix:
```ios
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip access-list extended GUEST-IN
R1(config-ext-nacl)# no 35
R1(config-ext-nacl)# end
R1# show access-lists GUEST-IN
```

Repeat a new gateway ping and HTTP request, renew DHCP, and confirm a guest-initiated staff ping remains denied. Existing NAT rows may outlive the fault; evaluate new traffic and counters.

title: Branch clients reach HQ but lose external access
scenario: The branch still reaches HQ but cannot reach the external server. The approved edge design uses a default route through 203.0.113.2 and advertises it conditionally to R1. R2’s ISP interface is up/up and that next hop answers a connected ping. The following state was collected after maintenance.

exhibits.title: Representative R1 state
exhibits.text:
Neighbor 2.2.2.2: FULL
O 10.255.20.0/24 via 10.255.12.2
Gateway of last resort is not set

exhibits.title: Representative R2 state
exhibits.text:
router ospf 1
 default-information originate
Gi0/1 203.0.113.1/24 up/up
show ip route 0.0.0.0: network not in table
Approved next hop: 203.0.113.2

question: Which repair restores the documented conditional default design?
options: Add always to origination despite the missing route
Change R1’s VLAN gateways to the ISP address
Make R2’s ISP interface an OSPF area 0 peer
Restore the approved static default on R2
explanation: R2 has no default route, so default-information originate without always has nothing to advertise. HQ reachability and the FULL neighbor isolate the missing external route from the functioning internal routing relationship.
fix:
```ios
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.2
R2(config)# end
R2# show ip route 0.0.0.0
```

After OSPF convergence, verify R1 learns the default and repeat numeric/name HTTP from both clients. Restoring a route is necessary here but still does not by itself prove the external service is healthy.
